name: Request supplier quotes (RFQs) and compare them
summary: Sends a request for quote to each supplier for an item list, logs every reply in a register, and raises a purchase order once a person has awarded the job. Crons read and draft; a person approves every send and every authorised purchase order.

all.evidence: 10 of 21 supplier-RFQ discovery calls describe their process; 7 send RFQs by hand or by email

covered_by.need-identified: skill (the owner or estimator lists the items)
covered_by.specify-item: skill (items and specs go into the RFQ record)
covered_by.pick-suppliers: skill (suppliers go into the RFQ record)
covered_by.send-rfq: issue (one draft per supplier, each send queued for approval)
covered_by.chase-quotes: chase (chaser drafts to suppliers who have not replied, sends queued for approval)
covered_by.receive-quotes: replies (each reply logged to the register)
covered_by.compare-quotes: skill (prices compared from the register and the replies)
covered_by.check-like-for-like: skill (scope checked by the agent and the estimator)
covered_by.approve-award: person (sets the award on the RFQ record)
covered_by.raise-po: purchase-order (Xero draft, authorise queued for approval)
covered_by.record-keeping: issue, replies and purchase-order write the register

crons.name: issue
crons.summary: Drafts one RFQ per supplier for each new RFQ and queues each send for approval.

crons.name: replies
crons.summary: Logs each new supplier reply to an open RFQ in the register.

crons.name: chase
crons.summary: Drafts chasers to suppliers who have not replied when a chase is due, and queues each send for approval (22:00 UTC is 8 or 9 am in eastern Australia).

crons.name: purchase-order
crons.summary: Drafts the Xero purchase order for each awarded RFQ and queues its authorisation for approval.

draft_ops_note: Draft operations reach nobody outside the business: an email in Drafts, a row in the register, a purchase order in Xero with status DRAFT. Sending an RFQ or a chaser, and authorising a purchase order, are live operations and wait for a person.

microsoft-365.covers: RFQ emails as drafts, chasers, reply reading from the RFQ folder, Excel register rows; sends queued for approval

xero.covers: purchase order drafted in DRAFT, moved to AUTHORISED only on approval

gaps: Buildxact: runs RFQs, quote receipt and purchase orders in product (the evidence rates send-rfq, receive-quotes and raise-po as supported), but the kit maps only its sign-in. Its RFQ and purchase order endpoints are needed before an adapter can be built.
Procore and EstimateOne: captured in the platform evidence, but neither has a kit platform folder, so no operations are mapped.
ServiceM8 supplier and material lists are mapped in the kit but not used here: the evidence names no ServiceM8 RFQ step.
Writing the RFQ record (items, suppliers, needed-by date) into the store has no CLI command yet. tools/workflow.ts is core and is not edited by this workflow.
Recording an award (the supplier, its Xero ContactID and the agreed unit prices) also has no CLI command yet. Until one exists, the CRM shell or a person writes it to the RFQ record.
Comparing prices, checking like-for-like scope and negotiating are judgment steps for the agent skill and the estimator. The crons never parse or rank a price.
Supplier award sign-off is not documented in the platform evidence. The award is a person's decision recorded on the RFQ record.
Delivery follow-up, late-delivery chasing and receipt matching have no mapped operations in this kit.
Every adapter is docs-only until a sandbox mailbox and a Xero demo company prove it.
